title: Moon base: fourteen days of night (one take; colours put back together, black sky, a true skyline)
note: Nov 24, seventh version. One camera take, no cut and no transition effect, 25.0 s. Script and voice as before; in the sound only the pause before the hit changed (the music no longer drops to full silence). Sources for the sky, the date, the place and the astronaut are in the notes of moonbase-v16.json and moonbase-v17.json. New here (specs/night_v18_one.json): the source's lens colour shift is measured on its own hard edges and undone (colour_shift.py); its blue lens glare is read from its own sky and taken off sky and ground, so the sky is black by day and only a white glow close round the Sun stays; the skyline is traced by hand and followed, so no star, glow or sky colour is drawn on the unlit far ridge; camera moves get up to speed, hold it and slow (top speed 10 px a frame, was 15), with a shorter shutter; sharpening is the finest band only, sized from the blur measured on the source; with the Sun in view there are no stars and no points of light in orbit; the Sun sinks toward the ridge while the ridge's shadow crosses the plain, is behind the ridge through the night and ends half hidden on the crest (spec key sun_drop; the source's Sun never moves); the brightest sunlit ground is brought down so the Sun is the brightest thing in view; the astronaut (now cut from NASA's 4K frames at 0.48 of their size) stands in sunlight with a lit rim, as does the top of the rock in front of him, while the plain below is in the ridge's shadow; at night the ground carries no Sun shadows, under any lamp; the travelling shadow's edge has the pointed fingers a peaked skyline casts; exhaust is a wide soft fan; the Earth's face is crisper and its gaps are filled; small figures have the proportions measured on NASA photograph AS11-40-5903, some kneel, and the walkers leave trodden ground. Removed: dust rising behind the ridge, a light pool on ground hidden by the ridge, the second lander's separate path (it now comes in along the line the first one lands on, so the video loops). Ours as before: the travelling shadow and its timing (hours shown in seconds), the night's level, every lamp, the landers, the small people, grain and lens fall-off. Credit NASA; NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio (Deep Star Maps 2020; Gaia DR2: ESA/Gaia/DPAC); NASA GIBS/Worldview (VIIRS, Suomi NPP; Black Marble); star positions HYG database (CC BY-SA 4.0). Sound effects are synthesised (sfx.py).

shots.job: This shot follows one night at the base in a single take: the Sun low over the ridge as a lander comes in and the ridge's shadow crosses the base; lamps, helmet lamps and stars in the dark under a crescent Earth; first light on the high ridge and across the plain; the shadow coming back as the camera returns to the Sun and a second lander arrives. So the viewer lives through the night the sentences describe. (NASA concept animation; everything listed in the note added)

lines.say: On most of the Moon, night lasts about fourteen days. Small landers have survived it by mostly shutting down.
A crew can't do that. Life support has to keep running, and no base has yet run through a lunar night.
text: Life support has to keep running,
